facts.text: New Blaine began as Blaine, named for James G., a pioneer who helped settle the Arkansas River Valley.
After the 1820s treaties removed the Osage and Cherokee, settlers from the east began farming the fertile lands that would become New Blaine.
When the Fort Smith, Subiaco & Eastern Railroad reached the area in 1920, the town’s commercial core moved south of Little Shoal Creek to sit beside the tracks.
In 1922 masons Aaron Moore, John Friga, and Freeborn Lasater built a row of native stone shops and a bank along Main Street, giving New Blaine its distinctive look.
The 1896 Jim and Lizzie Bell Horn House and the 1909 Iven and Alberta Horn Burnham House, both on the National Register, showcase the town’s vernacular architecture.
New Blaine sits in eastern Logan County, where Little Shoal Creek feeds into an arm of Lake Dardanelle on the Arkansas River.
